occult_infection_sepsis.clinical_definition: Select if the patient exhibits subtle temperature shifts (skin temp delta > +0.8°C), resting tachycardia exceeding Liebermeister's rule (+8.5 bpm/°C), nocturnal cough spikes, or acute mobility slowdown indicating an occult infection (UTI, aspiration pneumonia, or tropical fevers).

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Early or mild temperature/heart rate deviation without acute distress. Focus on oral temperature check, hydration, and confusion screening.
caregiver_checklist: Check your oral temperature with a digital thermometer under your tongue for 60 seconds
Drink a glass (250ml) of warm water or ORS to stay well hydrated
Take a quiet moment to sit down, rest, and note if you feel feverish, dizzy, or fatigued

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Confirmed fever, sustained resting tachycardia (>15 bpm over baseline), or symptoms persisting >48h. Requires stat home phlebotomy and urine tests.
caregiver_checklist: Rest comfortably seated in a well-ventilated room
Have your health records and recent prescriptions ready for the home phlebotomist visit
Keep well hydrated with warm fluids while awaiting your home test

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: High fever with altered mental status, severe breathlessness, rigors, or signs of septic shock. Immediate emergency transfer required.
caregiver_checklist: Sit or lie down in a comfortable resting position immediately
Call 108 ambulance right away or have someone transport you to the nearest casualty
Alert your primary caregiver or family member immediately

respiratory_hypoxemia_osa.clinical_definition: Select if the patient shows nocturnal SpO2 desaturations (<92%), frequent acoustic snoring events, tachypnea (>20 RPM), or daytime lethargy suggestive of Obstructive Sleep Apnea or cardiopulmonary strain.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Borderline nocturnal SpO2 dips (92-94%) or occasional snoring. Focus on head-of-bed elevation, sleeping posture, and spot checking.
caregiver_checklist: Prop up your head and upper body with an extra pillow (about 30°) to keep your airways open
Try sleeping on your side rather than flat on your back tonight
Take a spot-check of your oxygen with your fingertip oximeter while sitting comfortably upright

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Sustained nighttime hypoxemia (SpO2 nadir <92% across multiple nights) with acoustic snoring. Requires Home Sleep Apnea Test (HSAT).
caregiver_checklist: Note if you feel morning headaches, dry mouth, or daytime sleepiness
Perform regular daytime oxygen checks while seated upright
Keep your bedroom well ventilated and prepare for your home sleep study device delivery

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Severe hypoxemia (SpO2 <88% during day or sustained), severe respiratory distress, stridor, or cyanosis. Immediate emergency intervention.
caregiver_checklist: Sit completely upright immediately in a supportive chair
Use your prescribed emergency home oxygen if available (2 L/min via nasal cannula)
Call 108 emergency ambulance or head to the nearest emergency room immediately

cardiorenal_fluid_balance.clinical_definition: Select if the patient shows rapid weight gain (>1.5 kg in 3 days), loss of nocturnal HR dipping, frequent awakenings/nocturia, or lab indicators of worsening eGFR/creatinine.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Mild fluid drift or minor weight fluctuation. Focus on morning weigh-ins, ankle checks, and sodium tracking.
caregiver_checklist: Step on your weighing scale first thing in the morning (after using the bathroom, before breakfast)
Gently press your fingers against your ankles or shins for 5 seconds to check for any swelling
Keep your salt intake light today and stay mindful of your fluid intake

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Confirmed weight gain (>1.5 kg in 3 days) or laboratory decline in eGFR/kidney function. Requires stat renal & electrolyte panel.
caregiver_checklist: Measure your blood pressure while seated and after standing to check for any dizziness
Keep a written list of your daily heart and blood pressure medicines handy
Rest comfortably with your legs elevated on a footstool while awaiting home lab collection

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Acute congestive decompensation, severe shortness of breath when lying flat (orthopnea), frothy sputum, or hypertensive crisis. Immediate transfer required.
caregiver_checklist: Sit completely upright with your legs hanging over the side of the bed to ease breathing
Do NOT drink extra fluids right now
Call 108 ambulance immediately or have someone rush you to emergency casualty

sarcopenia_fall_prevention.clinical_definition: Select if the patient shows cautious shuffling cadence (<60 spm), prolonged sit-to-stand transitions (>15s), severe sleep debt with high step counts, or sudden mobility collapse.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Mild gait slowing or temporary fatigue after poor sleep. Focus on home environmental hazard removal and assistive footwear.
caregiver_checklist: Make sure walking pathways in your room are clear of loose rugs, clutter, or cords
Keep a nightlight or bedside lamp on if getting up in the dark
Wear non-skid supportive slippers or footwear inside (avoid walking in bare socks)

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Chronic cadence slowing (<65 spm for 2 weeks), near-falls, or sarcopenic decline. Requires home physiotherapy assessment.
caregiver_checklist: Take your time when moving between sitting and standing, and hold onto sturdy support
Notice if any knee, hip, or back stiffness is slowing your natural walking pace
Wear comfortable, loose clothing for your upcoming home physiotherapy assessment

secondary_cta.label: Order Vitamin D3 & Bone Mineral Labs

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Suspected fall, sudden inability to bear weight, severe hip/back pain, or head impact. Immediate emergency triage.
caregiver_checklist: If you have fallen or feel severe pain, stay still and do NOT attempt to get up abruptly
Call out for help or tap your emergency button to alert family and emergency services (108)
Keep warm with a light blanket while waiting for emergency assistance

cardio_autonomic_strain.clinical_definition: Select if the patient shows blunted heart rate recovery (<12 bpm at 1 min), reverse nocturnal dipping, widening pulse pressure (>60 mmHg), or blood pressure escalation.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Subtle autonomic drift or mild blood pressure elevation (Stage 1). Focus on orthostatic cautions and relaxation.
caregiver_checklist: Sit on the edge of your bed for 60 seconds before standing up to avoid dizziness
Avoid very hot showers or rushing right after waking up
Re-measure your sitting blood pressure and pulse after 30 minutes of restful sitting

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Sustained Stage 2 Hypertension, non-dipping night HR profile, or blunted HR recovery. Requires at-home ECG / Holter and cardiology review.
caregiver_checklist: Log your morning and evening blood pressure and pulse in your app diary
Avoid strenuous physical exertion and rest in a cool, comfortable environment
Keep your skin clean and dry before the home ECG / Holter technician arrives

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Hypertensive urgency (BP >= 180 mmHg with headache), acute chest pressure, radiation to jaw/left arm, or sudden syncope. Immediate emergency dispatch.
caregiver_checklist: Sit down in a comfortable chair immediately and loosen any tight clothing around your neck and chest
If you have prescribed SOS emergency cardiac tablets (e.g., Sorbitrate/Aspirin), take as advised by your doctor
Call 108 cardiac emergency ambulance immediately

sleep_metabolic_dysregulation.clinical_definition: Select if the patient shows deep sleep (Stage 5) depletion (<45 mins) coupled with morning hyperglycemia (>130 mg/dL), high glycemic variability, or RCV-confirmed HbA1c worsening.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Isolated night of poor deep sleep with expected mild morning insulin resistance. Focus on breakfast portion control and post-meal stroll.
caregiver_checklist: Have a wholesome, protein-rich breakfast (such as besan chilla, eggs, or sprouted moong)
Take a gentle 10 to 15-minute walk after eating to help balance your blood sugar
Check your blood sugar 2 hours after your meal with your home glucometer

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Frequent morning spikes, postprandial surges (>180 mg/dL), or rising HbA1c trend. Requires comprehensive metabolic lab review.
caregiver_checklist: Record your fasting and 2-hour post-meal blood sugar levels in your health log
Maintain consistent meal times and stay well hydrated with plain water
Keep your glucometer readings handy for your upcoming doctor or diabetes educator review

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Critical hypoglycemia (<54 mg/dL) with confusion/sweating OR severe hyperglycemia (>250 mg/dL with ketones/vomiting). Immediate emergency protocol.
caregiver_checklist: If your blood sugar is below 70 mg/dL and you feel shaky, immediately drink 1/2 cup fruit juice or 3 tsp sugar in water
Re-check your blood glucose in 15 minutes
If you feel faint, severely dizzy, or readings remain critical, call 108 medical emergency immediately

geriatric_polypharmacy.clinical_definition: Select if the pattern suggests adverse drug events, medication non-adherence, drug-vital interactions (e.g. sudden bradycardia post beta-blocker), or Beers criteria contraindications.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: Missed doses or minor scheduling confusion. Focus on pill-box reconciliation and audio reminders.
caregiver_checklist: Check your weekly pill box against your doctor's latest prescription
Double check if you took your evening medicines yesterday or if any were missed
Keep your medicines and water bottle within easy reach on your bedside table

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Suspected drug interaction, daytime dizziness, anticholinergic confusion, or multiple missed doses. Requires clinical pharmacist / GP review.
caregiver_checklist: Gather all your prescription boxes, syrups, and vitamins in one tray for doctor review
Write down any side effects, nausea, or dizziness you noticed after taking your medicines
Never stop or change prescribed doses on your own without consulting your doctor

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Acute drug toxicity, severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis, facial swelling), profound bradycardia (<45 bpm), or collapse following medication. Immediate transfer.
caregiver_checklist: Stop taking any further medication doses immediately
Keep the medicine strips or bottles right beside you so doctors know exactly what was taken
Call 108 emergency services immediately or have family take you to casualty

wellness_vitality_reinforcement.clinical_definition: Select if the patient's vitals are stable, goals are met (e.g. brisk cadence >=85 spm, active hours >=8), or chronic conditions are well-controlled.

level_1_bedside_triage.definition: All vitals stable and within target range. Reinforce positive habits and longevity milestones.
caregiver_checklist: Take pride in keeping up your consistent walking pace and restful sleep
Keep up your regular morning walks and drink plenty of fluids
Review your monthly progress report on your dashboard

level_2_diagnostic_investigation.definition: Stable chronic maintenance with upcoming annual preventive wellness checks.
caregiver_checklist: Check if your routine annual preventive blood tests are due this quarter
Plan your health goals and daily step targets for the upcoming month

level_3_acute_emergency.definition: Fallback emergency redirect if an urgent flag unexpectedly co-occurs.
caregiver_checklist: Take a restful seat and check how you are feeling
Contact your family doctor or emergency services (108) if sudden acute discomfort arises
Keep your recent health records and emergency contacts readily accessible
